sections.title: A computer as an information-processing system
sections.text:
A computer combines physical devices and instructions to transform represented data. Input supplies data or control, processing executes operations, output communicates results and storage retains information. These functions interact continuously: a browser reads stored instructions, receives network input, processes data and updates the screen. An information system also includes people, procedures, data quality and organizational purposes.

**Scientific definition.**

A computer is a programmable electronic device that accepts data, executes instructions, produces results and can store information. Four familiar operations describe much of its activity:

**Input → Processing → Output → Storage**

Modern computers also communicate extensively with other computers.

**Data versus information.**

**Data:** Recorded values, symbols or measurements that may require interpretation.

**Information:** Data organized or interpreted so that it communicates meaning.

Example: `37.5` is a numerical value. `Body temperature: 37.5°C` provides a physical quantity and context. The same data may have different meanings depending on its unit, source and situation.

**Hardware.**

Hardware consists of the physical components of a computer. Examples include the processor, motherboard, memory chips, SSD, monitor and keyboard. Hardware operates through electronic circuits and other physical mechanisms.

**Software.**

Software consists of instructions and associated data that direct a computer's operations. Examples include operating systems, web browsers, text editors, databases and computer games.

**Hardware is the physical machinery; software tells the machinery what operations to perform.**

**Firmware.**

Firmware is software closely associated with controlling or initializing hardware. It is commonly stored in nonvolatile memory such as flash. Examples include computer UEFI firmware and firmware within routers or printers. Firmware is software, even though it is stored inside physical hardware.

Input devices include keyboards, touch sensors, scanners, cameras and measurement instruments. Output devices include displays, speakers and printers. Some devices perform both functions, such as a touchscreen. Interfaces and buses transfer addresses, data and control signals between components. An interrupt allows an event to request processor attention through a defined handler rather than requiring continuous checking of every device.

sections.title: Processing, memory and storage
sections.text:
**the CPU.**

CPU stands for **Central Processing Unit**. It executes machine instructions and coordinates much of a computer's processing. It performs arithmetic, logical operations, decision-making based on instructions and control of data movement. The CPU is not the same thing as the entire computer.

**Main CPU components.**

| Component | Function |
|---|---|
| Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) | Performs arithmetic and logical operations |
| Control Unit (CU) | Coordinates instruction execution and control signals |
| Registers | Very small, fast storage locations inside the processor |
| Cache | High-speed memory reducing some slower memory accesses |
| Clocking mechanisms | Coordinate timing of synchronous operations |
| Execution units | Perform specialized integer, floating-point or other operations |

Some modern processors distribute these functions across multiple cores and sophisticated internal units.

**the fetch–decode–execute cycle.**

```text
1. Fetch — Retrieve an instruction from the instruction stream, commonly using memory/cache
   ↓
2. Decode — Determine which operation and operands are required
   ↓
3. Execute — Perform arithmetic, logic, load/store, branch or other operation
   ↓
4. Write back / update state — Store results, update architectural state and determine what executes next
   ↺ The cycle continues as the program executes.
```

**a clock cycle.**

A clock cycle is an interval in a synchronous processor's timing system. Clock frequency is measured in hertz. For example:

$$3\text{ GHz}=3\times10^9\text{ cycles per second}$$

**Important distinction:** A 3 GHz CPU does not necessarily execute exactly three billion instructions per second.

Instruction complexity, processor architecture, parallel execution, memory stalls and many other factors affect performance.

**RAM.**

RAM means **Random Access Memory**. It provides the main working memory used by active programs and the operating system. In ordinary computers, RAM is volatile: its contents are lost when electrical power is removed.

**ROM.**

ROM means **Read-Only Memory**. Traditionally, ROM refers to nonvolatile memory intended to retain data without electrical power. It is commonly associated with firmware and boot-related functions. Modern computers frequently use rewritable flash memory for firmware rather than literal permanently unchangeable mask ROM. Therefore, the statement "ROM can never be changed" is inaccurate as a general description of modern firmware storage.

**RAM versus ROM.**

| RAM | ROM / firmware storage |
|---|---|
| Usually volatile main memory | Nonvolatile |
| Holds active programs and data | Commonly stores firmware or fixed instructions |
| Frequently read and written during normal execution | Updates are less frequent and often controlled |
| High bandwidth, low latency | Purpose is persistence rather than ordinary working-memory performance |
| Example: DDR memory | Example: firmware flash |

**cache memory.**

A cache stores copies of frequently or recently accessed data and instructions closer to the processor's execution units. It reduces the average delay of accessing slower memory. Common cache levels include L1, L2 and L3. L1 is usually very small and fast. Higher cache levels generally have greater capacity but longer access times. The exact structure varies by processor.

**a cache hit.**

A cache hit occurs when the required data are found in the cache. A cache miss occurs when they are not present and must be retrieved from another memory level. Caches exploit two important patterns:

**Temporal locality:** Recently accessed information may be accessed again.

**Spatial locality:** Nearby memory locations may be accessed soon.

**SSD — Solid-State Drive.**

An SSD commonly stores information using NAND flash memory cells. These cells retain electrical charge states that represent information. SSDs do not need spinning platters or mechanically moving read heads. They generally provide substantially faster random access than HDDs, but performance, durability and cost depend on model and technology.

A program counter identifies the next instruction location in a simplified processor model, while registers hold operands and intermediate state. Multiple cores can execute separate instruction streams, and GPUs often favour high-throughput parallel workloads. Clock speed alone therefore cannot rank every computer's performance. Software structure, memory access, parallelism and the task's characteristics also matter.

HDDs store information magnetically on rotating media. SSDs commonly use flash with finite program–erase endurance, so controllers distribute writes through wear levelling. Error-correcting codes use redundant information to detect or correct selected error patterns. Neither wear levelling nor ECC eliminates every possible device failure; backups protect against different risks.

Virtual memory maps program-visible addresses to underlying memory resources and helps isolate processes. A valid page may temporarily be absent from RAM, causing a page fault and operating-system handling. Virtual memory does not create unlimited physical RAM. Excessive transfers to slower storage can seriously reduce performance.

sections.title: Operating systems, programs and algorithms
sections.text:
**an operating system.**

An operating system (OS) manages computer resources and provides services to programs. It coordinates processes, memory, files, devices and access controls. Examples include Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iOS.

**the kernel.**

The kernel is the core privileged part of an operating system. It manages critical functions such as process execution, memory protection and device access. Applications generally request services through system calls rather than directly controlling all hardware.

**a process.**

A process is an executing instance of a program, together with relevant state and allocated resources. An application can contain multiple processes. A process can contain multiple threads.

**a thread.**

A thread is a sequence of execution within a process. Threads within one process often share the same address space but possess their own execution state. This permits concurrent activities within a program.

An algorithm is a defined procedure for performing a task. A program expresses procedures in a form that can be translated or interpreted for execution. Compilers and interpreters are implementation approaches, and many systems combine them. Application software performs user tasks; system software manages underlying resources; firmware controls or initializes particular hardware.

Drivers provide operating-system interfaces to devices. File systems organize persistent data into files and directories with relevant metadata and permissions. Concurrency allows progress on multiple activities, but it does not necessarily mean every task runs at exactly the same instant. Correct coordination matters when processes or threads share resources.

sections.title: Binary, text, images and storage units
sections.text:
**Why is binary used.**

Digital electronic circuits can represent information using distinguishable electrical states. The binary number system uses two symbols:

$$\boxed{0\text{ and }1}$$

The physical implementation may use different voltage ranges, charge states or other mechanisms. Binary is particularly useful because electronic circuits can be designed to recognize and manipulate two logical states reliably.

**a bit.**

A **bit** is a binary digit. It can represent one of two logical values: 0 or 1. A **byte** conventionally consists of eight bits. For example: `10110010` contains eight bits.

**How does binary represent a number.**

Consider:

$$(1011)_2$$

Each position represents a power of two.

$$1(2^3)+0(2^2)+1(2^1)+1(2^0)$$

$$=8+0+2+1$$

$$\boxed{(1011)_2=11_{10}}$$

This explains numerical representation inside a digital computer.

Unicode assigns code points to characters; UTF-8 represents Unicode scalar values using one to four bytes. A visible symbol can also involve multiple code points, so a character count is not always equal to a byte count. Digital images store sampled picture elements, while audio stores sampled signal values. Sampling and quantization introduce distinct limits on representation.

One decimal megabyte, MB, is 1,000,000 bytes; one mebibyte, MiB, is 1,048,576 bytes. Thus 8,000,000 bytes is 8 MB or about 7.63 MiB. The binary number $1101_2$ is $8+4+1=13_{10}$. An uncompressed 1920 × 1080 image with three eight-bit colour channels requires $1920\times1080\times3=6,220,800$ bytes for pixel data, before metadata, padding or compression.

Lossless compression permits exact reconstruction of the encoded information. Lossy compression discards selected information to improve size or transmission trade-offs. Suitability depends on purpose: discarding detail acceptable for casual audio may be inappropriate for a scientific measurement archive. A file extension alone does not guarantee what information has been retained.

sections.title: Application software, business systems and social media
sections.text:
Word processors support document authoring, spreadsheets organize tabular data and calculations, presentation tools structure visual communication, and database applications manage organized records. Business software can coordinate accounting, inventory, payroll, customer relationships and supply chains. Enterprise resource planning integrates several functions around shared data and processes. A software package is useful only when its records, permissions and workflows fit the organization's actual requirements.

An information system combines hardware, software, data, people and procedures. A transaction-processing system records routine events, while management reports aggregate data for operational decisions. A dashboard can display indicators, but accurate visualization cannot compensate for inaccurate or incomplete input. Data validation, clear definitions and accountable correction processes are therefore part of system design.

Social media websites enable users to create profiles, publish material and interact through networks, groups or feeds. Their infrastructure combines databases, content storage, communication protocols and ranking systems. Recommendations often depend on predicted engagement rather than a scientific assessment of truth. Repetition, popularity and a verified account label therefore do not independently establish a claim's accuracy.

Privacy settings control some sharing, while the service may still process data according to its architecture and policies. Account security, consent, careful handling of location information and source checking matter for responsible use. Social media can disseminate weather warnings and health information quickly, but urgent messages should preserve the issuing authority, date, location and verification trail. A cropped screenshot or repost can remove precisely the context needed to interpret it.

questions.prompt: Which description best identifies a digital computer?

options.A: A machine used exclusively for arithmetic
options.B: A programmable system that processes digital data according to instructions
options.D: A device that only stores printed documents

questions.explanation: A digital computer executes instructions to process represented data and can store and communicate information.

questions.prompt: The physical components of a computing system are collectively called:

options.A: Hardware

questions.explanation: Hardware includes tangible components such as processors, memory chips and input/output devices.

questions.prompt: Which CPU component mainly performs arithmetic and logical operations?

options.A: SSD

questions.explanation: The Arithmetic Logic Unit performs arithmetic and bitwise/logical operations.

questions.prompt: In a simplified processor model, the Program Counter normally:

options.A: Stores every file permanently
options.D: Identifies the next instruction in the execution sequence

questions.explanation: The Program Counter holds an instruction address or analogous architectural state identifying the next instruction.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best represents a simplified instruction cycle?

options.A: Fetch → Decode → Execute → Update

questions.explanation: Processors fetch instructions, decode their meaning, execute operations and update architectural state.

questions.prompt: Why does a 3 GHz clock frequency not guarantee three billion instructions executed per second?

options.A: Every processor executes one instruction every minute
options.B: Clock frequencies only measure storage capacity
options.C: Instruction throughput also depends on architecture, stalls and parallel execution
options.D: All processors have identical instruction sets

questions.explanation: An instruction may require different resources and timing, and processors can overlap execution.

questions.prompt: Which description of CPU and GPU is most accurate?

options.A: Both are identical names for RAM
options.B: A CPU handles diverse general operations while GPUs are often optimized for high-throughput parallel computation
options.C: A GPU is exclusively an output monitor

questions.explanation: CPUs and GPUs have different architectural strengths; GPUs are widely used for graphics and many ML workloads.

questions.prompt: Which storage is usually volatile in a conventional computer?

options.A: HDD

questions.explanation: Ordinary RAM loses stored information without electrical power.

questions.prompt: What is a cache hit?

options.A: The required data are found in the cache
options.B: A computer has suffered a physical impact

questions.explanation: A cache hit occurs when a processor's requested information is already present in the relevant cache.

questions.prompt: Which modern storage technology commonly uses NAND flash without mechanical disk platters?

options.A: Optical tape

questions.explanation: Solid-state drives commonly use semiconductor flash memory and have no rotating disk platters.

questions.prompt: Which statement about ROM and firmware is correct?

options.A: Firmware must disappear when power is removed
options.B: Modern firmware is commonly kept in nonvolatile flash memory and may be updateable
options.C: ROM is always faster than all CPU registers

questions.explanation: Contemporary systems often use nonvolatile, rewritable flash memory for UEFI and other firmware.

questions.prompt: Virtual memory principally provides:

options.A: Unlimited additional physical RAM at no cost
options.B: A replacement for all CPU registers
options.D: Managed virtual address spaces and memory mapping

questions.explanation: Virtual memory provides address-space abstraction and protection, not unlimited free physical memory.

questions.prompt: Which part of an operating system handles core privileged resource management?

options.A: Kernel

questions.explanation: The OS kernel performs core privileged operations including memory and process management.

questions.prompt: A process differs from a thread because:

options.A: Every thread must have its own operating system
options.C: Threads are execution units commonly sharing resources within one process
options.D: A thread is a physical storage disk

questions.explanation: Threads within a process commonly share an address space while retaining individual execution state.

questions.prompt: Which task is commonly performed by a device driver?

options.A: Replacing the CPU's physical transistors
options.B: Providing an interface between operating-system software and a hardware device
options.C: Converting all images into paper automatically

questions.explanation: Drivers help operating systems communicate with particular hardware devices.

questions.prompt: A byte conventionally contains:

options.A: 2 bits

questions.explanation: One byte conventionally consists of eight bits.

questions.prompt: What decimal value does the binary number 1011 represent?
Which statement correctly describes Unicode and UTF-8?

options.A: They are two kinds of RAM
options.B: Unicode is only for English letters
options.C: Unicode defines characters; UTF-8 is one encoding of Unicode text

questions.explanation: Unicode assigns character identities/code points, while UTF-8 encodes them into bytes.

questions.prompt: Which distinction between lossless and lossy compression is correct?

options.A: Lossless necessarily destroys image pixels
options.B: Lossless supports exact reconstruction, while lossy may discard information
options.C: Lossy can never reduce file size

questions.explanation: Lossless compression retains all required original information; lossy compression deliberately reduces some information.

questions.prompt: A computer algorithm is best understood as:

options.A: Only a physical CPU chip
options.D: A well-defined procedure for performing a task

questions.explanation: Algorithms are procedures; programs implement them in executable form.

questions.prompt: Why is a national information system more than a collection of computers?

options.A: Computers are incapable of storing information
options.B: Information systems do not require people
options.D: It integrates technology with data, procedures, people and organizational purposes

questions.explanation: Information systems combine technical and organizational components to process useful information.

questions.prompt: An input device signals the processor that an I/O operation needs attention. Which mechanism can interrupt ordinary instruction flow to service the event?

options.A: Protein translation

questions.explanation: Interrupt mechanisms allow hardware or software events to request processor attention through defined handler routines.

questions.prompt: A program accesses a valid virtual-memory page that is not currently present in main RAM. Which event may occur?

options.A: The CPU turns into an SSD
options.C: A page fault followed by operating-system memory handling

questions.explanation: Page faults can trigger loading or mapping of memory pages; not every page fault represents an invalid access.

questions.prompt: Why does error-correcting-code memory contain additional coded information?

options.A: To detect and correct selected memory-bit errors
options.B: To eliminate all electric power consumption

questions.explanation: ECC uses redundancy to detect and often correct certain error patterns, depending on its code.

questions.prompt: Wear leveling in a flash-based SSD is designed chiefly to:

options.A: Move every file into RAM permanently
options.D: Distribute writes to reduce concentrated flash-cell wear

questions.explanation: Wear-leveling algorithms spread programming/erase activity among flash blocks to improve endurance.

questions.prompt: Why can a UTF-8-encoded text character occupy more than one byte?

options.A: UTF-8 is always a sixteen-bit fixed-width code
options.B: UTF-8 uses a variable-length byte representation for Unicode code points
options.C: All characters are stored as image pixels
options.D: Characters are converted into radio waves before storage

questions.explanation: UTF-8 uses one to four bytes for Unicode scalar values, depending on the code point.

analytical.prompt: Explain the architecture of a digital computer and critically analyze the roles of the CPU, memory, storage and operating system.
analytical.answer_html:
Introduction

A digital computer is a programmable electronic system that represents information in digital form and processes instructions through hardware and software. Its major functional components include input/output interfaces, processing units, memory and nonvolatile storage.

CPU

The central processing unit executes instructions. The arithmetic logic unit performs arithmetic and logical operations. Control logic coordinates instruction processing. Registers hold information required during execution.

Instruction cycle

A simplified instruction cycle includes fetching, decoding, execution and updating processor state. Modern processors may perform multiple internal operations in parallel or out of order to improve performance.

Memory

RAM provides active working memory. Cache reduces the average latency of repeatedly accessing relevant instructions and data. Registers provide very fast local storage. ROM or flash-based firmware storage maintains important initialization instructions.

Secondary storage

SSDs and HDDs retain programs and files without continuous electrical power. SSDs generally provide faster random access than mechanical hard drives.

Operating system

The operating system manages processes, memory, devices, files and permissions. It provides services that enable applications to use computing resources safely and efficiently.

Conclusion

Computer performance and reliability depend on the coordinated functioning of hardware, firmware and software. No single component can perform the complete role of a digital computer.

analytical.prompt: Differentiate RAM, ROM, cache and secondary storage. Explain why modern systems use a memory hierarchy.
analytical.answer_html:
Introduction

Computer memory and storage technologies vary in speed, cost, capacity and persistence. Modern systems use multiple levels to balance these characteristics.

Registers

Registers are very small and fast storage locations within the processor. They hold operands, addresses and intermediate results.

Cache

Cache retains selected frequently or recently needed instructions and data. Cache hits reduce accesses to slower memory.

RAM

RAM stores active programs and working data. Ordinary RAM is volatile and loses its contents when power is removed.

ROM and firmware storage

ROM historically refers to nonvolatile storage for fixed instructions. Modern systems often store updateable firmware in nonvolatile flash.

Secondary storage

HDDs and SSDs store programs and files persistently. HDDs use rotating magnetic media. SSDs commonly use NAND flash.

Why multiple levels are necessary

Very fast memory is often relatively expensive per unit of capacity. Slower storage can offer much larger capacity. A hierarchy allows frequently needed information to remain closer to execution units while less frequently accessed data stay in larger storage.

Conclusion

Memory hierarchy is a fundamental design approach that reduces average access cost while preserving sufficient storage capacity.
